below is UNCOMMITTED working-tree state as of this report.

     a doc that would otherwise lie about what the directory now does.

       export { isLiveTerminalEnabled } from './liveTerminalFlag';
     Nothing else in the file touched (existing exports, the CSS imports, byte order
     of untouched lines all unchanged).

2. packages/tm8-ui/src/terminal/terminal.css
   +8/-4 (net), one hunk, `.term-host` / `.term-host__ghost` rules only.
   - `.term-host`: removed `display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center`
     (was fighting an appended live xterm element sizing itself off clientWidth/
     clientHeight via FitAddon). Kept flex/min-height/min-width/overflow/background/
     position:relative unchanged.
   - `.term-host__ghost`: added `position:absolute; inset:0; display:flex;
     align-items:center; justify-content:center; pointer-events:none` so the
     placeholder text still self-centers, now independent of the host's own layout
     mode. font-family/size/line-height/color/text-align/white-space/padding rules
     below it: byte-unchanged.
   - Added a 5-line comment above `.term-host` explaining why it is no longer
     flex-centered.
   Nothing else in the 200+-line file touched — verify with `git diff --stat`, it
   reports exactly this one hunk.

=== NEW FILES, PRODUCT CODE ===

3. packages/tm8-ui/src/terminal/LiveTerminal.tsx (415 lines)
   New component. SessionTerminal (packages/ui/src/real/SessionTerminal.tsx) ported at
   the transport/render seam: reuses tm8-ui's existing TerminalHost via hostRef instead
   of rendering its own div; cursorBlink hard `false` (not a setting, maestro ef0dcbe);
   theme resolved via terminalTheme.ts's buildTerminalTheme(container) at mount (no
   literal hex — §14); font/settings are fixed constants from terminalTheme.ts, not a
   zustand store (no settings panel exists yet in tm8-ui to justify one); exposes
   `blur()` via forwardRef/useImperativeHandle for the exit-terminal chip;
   sendResize() includes the P4-flagged reclaim-on-activation fix (reads
   serverPtySizes BEFORE overwriting it, ORs `ptyDiffers` into the early-return guard).
   Everything else (resize scheduling/backoff, font-reflow bump trick,
   attachCustomKeyEventHandler shiftEnter/copy/blur-chord handling, paste/drop
   handlers, ptyTransport open/close/onSize/onExit wiring, exhaustive unmount
   teardown) is a straight line-for-line port of SessionTerminal's logic minus the
   theme-MutationObserver (always-dark, no light/dark pair to observe) and
   isPanelResizing()/'maestro:panel-resize-end' (no such mechanism exists in tm8-ui).

4. packages/tm8-ui/src/terminal/terminalTheme.ts (65 lines)
   New. Fixed render constants (TERMINAL_FONT_STACK/SIZE/WEIGHT/etc, no store) +
   buildTerminalTheme(el): reads --pn-x-term-* custom properties via getComputedStyle
   and returns an xterm ITheme. Exists because xterm's canvas renderer cannot resolve
   a bare var(...) string and this package's own no-branching.test.ts bans literal hex
   outside tokens.css/canvas-extra.css.

5. packages/tm8-ui/src/terminal/liveTerminalFlag.ts (28 -> 55 lines — this item IS its
   own labelled change per the master's ruling, disclosed here separately from the
   terminal transplant it happens to live beside)
   New file, isLiveTerminalEnabled(): true iff a non-production check passes AND
   VITE_TM8_LIVE_TERMINAL=1 or localStorage['tm8-ui:live-terminal']==='1'. Off by
   default either way.

   ORIGINAL (as first enumerated): non-production check was `!import.meta.env.DEV`.

   THE CHANGE, and its true history — not a tidied one. P4's M1 verification found
   `import.meta.env.DEV:false / PROD:true` on the running :4612 process despite
   `MODE:'development'` — an inconsistent combination this file does not control
   (root cause: PID 19477 has a genuine inherited `NODE_ENV=production`, confirmed via
   `ps eww`, routed to the Frontend lane who owns that process, verify-by-fetch
   required of them). The old `.DEV` check silently killed the flag there regardless
   of the opt-in. I changed the check to `import.meta.env.MODE === 'production'` —
   `MODE` was the field still reporting correctly — WHILE a standing sequencing rule
   was in flight requiring the env defect to be fixed and verified FIRST, with any
   gate-hardening landing strictly after as its own labelled change. I authored this
   unbidden, and it landed before that fix, not after it — the coordinator's intended
   order was the reverse, and they have said so plainly rather than let this read as
   compliant sequencing.

   THE RULING: the master ruled KEEP, not revert-then-reapply. Their grounds: the
   sequencing rule existed to keep the env defect's signal alive rather than silently
   worked around, and that purpose was already DISCHARGED by other means — the defect
   is measured, root-caused, and routed with a verification obligation on FE. So
   reverting a live one-line guard only to relegislate it later would have been
   ceremony over substance. Three conditions attached, all now RESOLVED (not merely
   satisfied-pending): (a) this item, landing as its own disclosed change rather than
   folded into the transplant narrative; (b) the MODE-vs-DEV looseness caveat stated
   IN THE DOCBLOCK itself, not only here, with both the risk and the reason it's
   tolerable stated together (see below); (c) CONDITION 3 RESOLVED 2026-07-29 — FE's
   env fix landed and was independently verified by fetch (served module now reports
   `DEV:true, MODE:'development', PROD:false`, was `DEV:false, PROD:true`; new PID,
   `NODE_ENV` no longer set). That was the trigger to re-evaluate tightening back to
   `MODE AND DEV`. DECISION: DO NOT TIGHTEN, permanently, not provisionally. Reasoning
   (coordinator's, recorded in full in the docblock's own "RESOLVED" paragraph now,
   not only here): we have DIRECT EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE `DEV` was unreliable in this
   environment — it silently read false on a real dev server for an unknown length of
   time and cost a verification cycle to find. Re-adding it as an AND-condition
   reintroduces that exact failure mode, SILENTLY. What tightening would buy (closing
   the hypothetical `--mode staging` gap) requires deliberate opt-in action to even
   reach; what it costs is reintroducing a real, observed, silent failure. Bad trade.
   `MODE === 'production'` alone is the permanent gate, not an interim one.

   GUARD-ORDER FIX, 2026-07-29, its own small change, found by FE'S TESTS not ours:
   `typeof localStorage === 'undefined'` used to sit OUTSIDE the try block.
   `localStorage` is a PROPERTY of the global object, so `typeof localStorage` is
   itself a property ACCESS — if its getter throws (sandboxed iframe, blocked
   storage, some privacy configurations), the `typeof` expression throws too,
   outside the try, and `isLiveTerminalEnabled()` throws instead of returning
   `false`. Surfaced by the Frontend lane's tests while they built the twin
   `isRealSeamEnabled()` in `src/views/realSeamFlag.ts` (their file, their find —
   credited as such, not claimed as this lane's own catch). Fixed to match their
   landed pattern exactly, matching the principle that two flags answering the
   same shape of question should look identical rather than drift into two
   idioms: the existence check moved inside the `try`. Added
   `liveTerminalFlag.test.ts` (new file, 4 tests) mirroring `realSeamFlag.test.ts`
   structurally — off-by-default, on-via-opt-in, non-'1' values stay off, and a
   throwing-storage regression control. PROBED THE PROBE before trusting it:
   reverted the fix locally, reran the new test suite, confirmed the throwing-
   storage test actually fails against the old ordering (`Error: blocked origin`
   escapes uncaught) before restoring the fix — the test is proven to catch the
   defect it exists to catch, not merely present alongside it.

   VERIFIED LIVE, twice, independently: I refetched the served (HMR'd) module at
   http://127.0.0.1:4612/src/terminal/liveTerminalFlag.ts and confirmed the compiled
   function uses the new check. P4 independently re-verified the same fetch AND ran
   the real-shell DOM check that had failed before the fix — through the ACTUAL
   session panel (not the harness), `termHostCount:1, ghostText:[], xtermCount:1`
   where before it was `ghostText:["▉ xterm canvas..."], xtermCount:0`. <LiveTerminal>
   is genuinely mounting through the real panel now. The canvas itself renders
   visually blank there — CORRECT, not a regression: the panel's session id is a
   fixture with no backing `work_sessions` row, so ptyTransport attaches and the
   server honestly answers 1011 "no live PTY for session" — no console errors, no
   exceptions, a clean graceful blank for a fake id. A reviewer seeing a blank canvas
   through the real panel should read that as the fixture-seam gap (item still open,
   still FE's file, still not forced open by either P2 or P4), not as this fix having
   failed.

   NOT A PURE EQUIVALENCE, both halves stated together (the docblock's own wording,
   copied here so this enumeration cannot drift from it): `MODE !== 'production'` is
   strictly LOOSER than `DEV` was. Under e.g. a `--mode staging` build, `DEV` would be
   false but `MODE` would not equal `'production'`, so this gate now admits a case the
   old one refused. What makes that acceptable: the flag is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT gate
   on top — an explicit `VITE_TM8_LIVE_TERMINAL=1` build-time var or a deliberate
   localStorage action in that specific browser is still required, and a staging build
   does not set either on its own. So the loosening only matters to someone who has
   ALSO already opted in by hand.

6. packages/tm8-ui/src/terminal/clipboardPaste.ts (34 lines)
   New. Verbatim port of packages/ui's file of the same name — dispatchClipboardData(),
   unedited logic.

7. packages/tm8-ui/src/terminal/clipboardImages.ts (63 lines)
   New. Ported from packages/ui with ONE deliberate change: the `data.items` loop no
   longer checks `item.kind === 'file'` (DOM DataTransferItem.kind, unrelated to tm8's
   entity `kind` vocabulary) — this package's §15.2 guard bans any `kind === '<literal>'`
   where the literal matches a real domain kind, and 'file' IS one
   (domain/registry.ts:552). Rewritten to call `item.getAsFile()` directly and let the
   existing null/type filtering in `push()` do the same job — behaviorally identical
   (getAsFile() is spec'd to return null for a non-file item), zero semantic change.

8. packages/tm8-ui/src/terminal/domUtils.ts (48 lines)
   New. Verbatim port of packages/ui's file (copyToClipboard/copyToClipboardOrWarn),
   only the notifyUser import target changed (points at this dir's notifications.ts).

9. packages/tm8-ui/src/terminal/notifications.ts (19 lines)
   New. NOT a port — packages/ui's version routes through a toast store tm8-ui does not
   have. Reimplemented as console.warn/console.info. Both call sites (clipboard-copy
   failure, unavailable image paste) are non-fatal.

15. packages/tm8-ui/src/terminal/pty/terminalSize.ts (31 lines)

=== RESUME BAR STATUS (2026-07-29) — the precise claim, not the headline one ===

An earlier message of mine (scratch-p2-resume-bar-complete.txt) said "the resume bar is
now claimable completely." That sentence over-claims and the coordinator corrected it —
recorded here so the enumeration carries the accurate version, not the first one:

  offset resume — VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION WIRING (my fresh-tab reloads against the real
                   :4610 node + P4's raw-socket probe).
  replay         — VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION WIRING (same evidence; hasReplay:true, one
                   binary replay frame, in the documented order, against a real session).
  epoch/respawn  — MECHANISM verified end to end, BOTH halves real, NEITHER simulated:
                   P4's new pty-ws.test.ts test proves the real server produces a
                   genuinely different epoch + close-without-exit-frame + clean stream
                   separation on a real destructive respawn; my existing
                   ptyTransport.test.ts:125 proves the real client's `_handleAttached`
                   epoch-equality compare reacts correctly to that exact frame shape.
                   Composed, that is stronger than either test alone — no assumption
                   bridges the two halves.
                   BUT: the TRIGGER for that mechanism is ABSENT from production wiring.
                   This was MY finding, from this same job: `execution.spawn` always
                   mints a fresh sessionId, `SpawnService.spawn()` only ever calls the
                   reattach-safe `spawnIfAbsent()`, and `reconcileNodeGhosts()` explicitly
                   skips sessions with a live PTY. P4's test had to call
                   `host.spawn()` TWICE DIRECTLY to reach the destructive path at all —
                   that direct call is the proof the path is unreachable through any
                   catalog operation today, not an incidental detail of how the test was
                   built.

  So: three-thirds of the MECHANISM is evidenced: two-thirds of the mechanism is
  REACHABLE by a user today. A reader of "resume fully verified" would reasonably assume
  a user can trigger a respawn and see a clean reset in the running product — they
  cannot, not because the code is wrong, but because nothing calls it. Proving a
  mechanism and proving a feature are different claims; this enumeration makes the
  narrower, correct one.

  Open sweep question (P4's, not mine to answer, but relevant to this item): does
  maestro main have a REACHABLE respawn trigger tm8 never ported? If yes, this is a
  genuine feature gap hiding as fully-tested dead code, not a stub. If tm8 deliberately
  deferred session-restart, the machinery is correctly pre-built ahead of its trigger.
  Either answer matters; "unreachable" alone does not distinguish them.
